title: Best AI Presentation Makers 2026: 17 Tools Tested Side by Side
summary: I tested 17 AI presentation makers side-by-side with the same prompt. Here's which ones produce clean PPT exports, which break, and which are worth paying for
body_text: Quick Verdict: Best AI Presentation Makers for 2026 Don't have time to read 5,000 words? Here's who wins: Use Case Winner Why Best AI presentation maker for enterprises Alai Full design system encoding, Agent Mode for clean and fast edits, existing template imports, clean PPTX export, API/A2A/MCP for deck creation at scale Best free AI presentation maker Gamma 400 credits free at signup, no card required Best AI presentation maker for design teams Chronicle / Canva Chronicle for widget-based interactive presenting; Canva for massive template library and all-in-one design ecosystem Best AI presentation maker for research-first decks Manus AI Claude 3.7 Sonnet with live web research and Gmail/Slack/Drive/Notion workspace integrations Best AI presentation maker for sales teams (analytics) Pitch Pitch Rooms bundle decks with supporting assets, plus slide-level engagement analytics for smarter follow-up Best AI presentation maker for Google Slides & PowerPoint users Plus AI Native add-on inside Google Slides and PowerPoint with Live Snapshots and saved prompts Best budget AI presentation software SlidesAI Pro plan under $10/month with 100+ language translation built in I tested 17 AI presentation makers with the same prompt, the same brand colours, and the same 10-slide deck topic. Some produced clean PowerPoint exports. Some broke on slide 3. Two ignored my brand guidelines entirely and made their own deck. This is what I found. What Is an AI Presentation Maker? An AI presentation tool uses artificial intelligence to automate slide creation: generating content from prompts, creating layouts, selecting images, and maintaining design consistency. Instead of starting from a blank slide, you: Provide a prompt ("Create a Series A pitch deck for an AI startup") Upload existing content (notes, PDFs, documents) Let the AI generate a first draft Edit and refine The best AI presentation software handle the 80% that's grunt work so you can focus on the 20% that matters: your message and narrative. Why Use an AI Presentation Maker? Save Hours on Every Deck Based on my benchmarks across the 15 tools in this article, moving from a text outline to a presentable first draft takes 3-6 minutes on average. Building the same deck manually in PowerPoint takes 2-4 hours. The time savings are front-loaded in structure and layout, the two parts AI handles best. Professional Design Without a Designer The best AI tools enforce design principles automatically: proper spacing, consistent fonts, visual hierarchy. You get professional output without needing to know what makes a slide look good. Keep Your Team On-Brand When everyone uses the same AI tool with brand guidelines, every deck looks like it came from the same company. No more "who designed this?" moments. How I Tested These 16+ AI Presentation Makers I ran every tool through the same test. Same prompt. Same content. Same brand colors. Same export targets. Here is exactly what I gave each AI presentation maker: "Create a 10-slide pitch deck using the following content. Keep the content on each slide exactly the same as the content I have shared. Structure: title, problem, market size, solution, product overview, traction, business model, competitive landscape, team, ask. Use a clean, professional theme suitable for an investor audience." I pasted the same source content into every tool. Then I exported each deck to PowerPoint 365 and opened it in Google Slides to check for formatting damage. Testing Criteria For Each AI Presentation Tool Every tool gets a score out of 100 based on five weighted criteria: Criterion What I tested Content and design accuracy How accurately does it replicate the content and design guidelines I uploaded Design quality of first draft How close is the first draft to the final draft PowerPoint and Google Slide export quality How well does it export as a PPTX and even Google Slide file Speed to presentable draft How long does it take to go from first to final draft Free tier and pricing value Is the tool worth your money and can it be tested freely before locking in on a paid plan? What I Did Not Include and Why I excluded AI presentation software with no public pricing and no self-serve trial. I excluded tools that have not shipped a meaningful update in the last 12 months. I excluded browser extensions that wrap ChatGPT and call themselves AI presentation makers without producing actual slides. The AI ppt tools below all passed the basic test: real product, real updates in 2026, real output. AI Presentation Maker Comparison: Features, Pricing & Output Examples Don't want to read the detailed review? Here's a quick summary of each tool's features, pricing and output. deck mode Design system (Team only) 60 mins Good (requires some formatting) $17/mo How Much Do AI Presentation Tools Cost? (The Real Math) The comparison table above shows headline pricing. It does not show what actually costs you when you start using these tools. After hours of testing, I kept a running list of the moments where the real bill did not match the advertised price. Some are minor. A few are dealbreakers depending on how you plan to pay. Here is the consolidated list, ranked roughly by how badly each one bites the budget. Tool The pricing trap What they do not tell you upfront Beautiful AI $45/month if you pay monthly, $12/month if you commit annually A 275% markup for not locking in a year. There is no middle ground. Plus AI No actual free tier The "free trial" is 7 days and requires a credit card upfront. Forget to cancel and you are on Basic at $15/month. Pitch Free plan credits are one-time, not monthly 100 AI credits at signup, then zero. The free plan technically stays free forever, but the AI features stop working after your first deck or two. Claude Design Brand consistency is locked to a 5-seat Team plan Design system setup requires Team Standard at $20/seat/month annual with a 5-seat minimum. Individual Pro at $17/month and Max at $100 to $200/month do not get it. If you signed up for Claude Pro expecting brand-aware decks, you cannot enable that without converting to a team account at $1,000+/year minimum. SlidesGPT The free plan does not let you download anything You can generate the deck, view it, share a link. Export to PPT, PDF, or Google Slides is paid-only at $10/month. You build it and cannot leave with it without paying. Napkin AI Editable export is paid-only Free plan exports PNG and PDF with a watermark. To get editable PowerPoint output, you need Plus at $9/month annual. Most reviews call Napkin "free" without flagging this. SlidesGPT (paid plans) Unused downloads do not roll over The $10/month Pro plan gives you 10 downloads per month. Use 6, lose 4 at the reset. The download count is metered, not banked. Claude Design No published credit counts or slide limits per tier Anthropic does not disclose exact credit or slide counts on any plan, including the $200/month Max 20x tier. Allowances are per user, not pooled at the org level. Budgeting for team usage is guesswork. Prezent.ai No self-serve trial or transparent pricing You cannot test the product without a sales call. Pricing is custom-quoted. Running an internal pilot takes weeks longer than any other tool in this list, and you commit to a contract before you know what you are paying. Prezi AI Plus plan does not include AI The $7/month Plus tier looks affordable until you realise AI generation is only on the $19/month Premium tier. The cheap plan is a non-AI Prezi subscription with a different name. A few of these are minor inconveniences. The ones that hurt most in practice are the ones that force you to commit money before you have tested the tool: Plus AI's credit card wall, Prezent's sales call, and Claude Design's 5-seat minimum for brand consistency. If you are picking a tool for a team or an organisation, Claude Design's 5-seat Team minimum is the most expensive surprise on this list for anyone who started on Claude Pro. The math goes from $17/month for one person to $1,000+/year minimum for the feature most teams actually need. It does not show up on the pricing page. It shows up the first time you try to enforce brand guidelines. How AI Presentation Tools Compare On The Same Prompt Most AI presentation maker round-ups cover features but none of them compare slide quality side-by-side using the exact same content. The slides showed in this section were all delivered as the first draft of each AI ppt maker with just the content given to the tools with basic instruction on design. Here's the exact prompt I used: "Create a 10-slide pitch deck using the following content. Keep the content on each slide exactly the same as the content I have shared. Structure: title, problem, market size, solution, product overview, traction, business model, competitive landscape, team, ask. Use a clean, professional theme suitable for an investor audience." Alai: Uses a Venn diagram to visualize the relationship between patient reality, payer reality, and outcomes. Clean layout with balanced spacing between the title and the visual element. Gamma: Restructures the same content into a three-column layout with an AI-generated background image. Dark theme adds visual contrast, though the columns leave limited breathing room for the text. Canva: Flat bullet list with a decorative graphic element in the corner. Content is consolidated under a single heading rather than structured into categories. Large amount of empty space in the lower half of the slide goes unused. Plus AI Content is well-organized into three labeled sections with clear paragraph descriptions. Readable structure, but minimal design - no visual elements, color differentiation, or hierarchy beyond text formatting. Reflects the design constraints of Google Slides as the underlying platform. Pitch Splits content into a two-column layout with a stock image. Only covers the patient perspective - payer reality and outcomes from the original content are added two separate slides. The paragraph-style body text is dense for a presentation slide. SlidesAI Condenses all content into a single paragraph summary, losing the structured breakdown of patient reality, payer reality, and outcomes. The AI-generated image - a workforce scale visual doesn't directly relate to the slide's content. Significant empty space on the left half of the slide goes unused. Prezi AI Breaks content into four labeled cards, which organizes the information well structurally. However, the body text within each card is too small to read comfortably in a presentation setting. The AI-generated background images - architectural renders of healthcare facilities - compete for attention with the text rather than supporting it. Title is placed on the right, reversing the expected reading flow. Chronicle Strong visual impact with a well-chosen stock image and clear title hierarchy. The four widget-style tags at the bottom surface key data points, but they read as labels rather than complete thoughts — "Preventable outcomes:" and "Extended waits:" are truncated without the actual details. The slide prioritizes atmosphere over information delivery. Gemini Clean two-column layout that preserves the patient and payer categories with key stats highlighted in color. Readable and well-structured, though visually plain - no imagery, no visual elements beyond basic card containers. Functional but closer to a document layout than a presentation slide. Napkin AI: Napkin AI doesn't generate a full slide from the prompt the way other tools do. I pasted the patient/payer comparison content into the editor, clicked the spark icon, and got six layout options for the same content. I chose the comparison table, which organizes the data into a three-column structure: characteristic, patient reality, and payer reality. The table presents the data accurately and the layout is clean, but it doesn't connect the findings. A viewer sees the two perspectives as separate columns without understanding how they create a shared problem. The headline "Mental Health Care Access Discrepancy" also undersells the urgency of what the data is showing. For content this heavy, a layout that visualizes the overlap and consequence between patient and payer reality would communicate the point faster, but none of the six options Napkin generated pushed in that direction. The data is all there. The visual logic to tie it together isn't. Genspark AI: Genspark's output here is visually ambitious but harder to read than it should be. The two-panel split between patient reality and payer reality, combined with the flow diagram at the bottom, gives the slide three distinct areas competing for attention at once. As an audience member, it's not immediately clear where to start. The patient panel and payer panel feel disconnected from each other, so the relationship between the two, which is the whole point of the slide, gets lost. The numerical emphasis is genuinely good: 3-6 months, 40M members, 10% of members driving 50% of spend are all surfaced clearly. But the layout asks the viewer to do the connecting work themselves rather than doing it for them. The flow diagram at the bottom is the right instinct but the truncated labels and unexplained color dots add confusion rather than clarity. Strong content, layout that needs a rethink. Manus AI: Manus structured the slide into four labeled sections across two panels: problem and patient reality on the left, result and payer reality on the right. The key stats made it through accurately: 3-6 month wait times, 40M members, 10% of members driving 50% of spend. The spend concentration bar chart in the payer reality panel is a good call, it turns a ratio into something visually immediate rather than leaving it as a text claim. The headline "The Crisis in Medicaid Behavioral Health Care" is also stronger than most tools produced for this slide. Where it falls short is the same place Genspark does: the two panels feel like two separate arguments rather than one connected problem. The causal link between patient reality and payer reality, that access gaps are what create the cost concentration, isn't shown anywhere on the slide. A viewer reads both panels and understands each one individually but has to make the connection themselves. The source citation at the bottom is a nice credibility touch that no other tool in this test included. NotGPT: NoteGPT was the only tool in this test that ignored the source content entirely. Instead of using the patient/payer slide content I provided, it ran its own research and generated a full 10-slide deck on mental health broadly. This slide is from that deck. The content is accurate in a general sense but has nothing to do with the specific Medicaid framing, the 40M members figure, the payer cost concentration, or any of the data points from the original prompt. On the design side, the two-panel layout is functional but entirely text-driven: two paragraph blocks sitting inside colored cards with no data visualization, no hierarchy beyond the subheadings, and no design elements that would hold attention in a live presentation. For a slide making the case that a mental health crisis exists, dense paragraph text is about the least persuasive format you could choose. When to Choose SlidesGPT You need a fast internal draft and will do a manual design pass yourself afterward You're a ChatGPT power user and want presentation generation inside your existing workflow via the plugin You're automating presentation creation at scale via API and need a simple, reliable generation pipeline Skip SlidesGPT if you need visual variety across slides, design quality that holds up in a client or investor setting, or content depth on short prompts without significant manual input. 17. Claude Design: Best AI Presentation Maker For One Off Visual Decks Category: Best for One-Off Branded Visual Decks Verdict: ★★★★☆ Claude Design is Anthropic's Labs tool for visual creation and probably one of the best ways to create decks via an LLM when compared to Gemini or Manus. You pick "Slide Deck" as your starting mode, create your own detailed branding system and answer four or five clarifying questions, and Claude builds a deck you can edit slide by slide. It's one of three ways Claude can natively build a presentation, and it produces the best-looking first draft of the three by a clear margin. I built the same 10-slide deck through Claude Design that I used to test every tool in this list. The typography is the thing that lands first. Display font for headlines, contrasting sans for body, mono for data labels, consistent across every slide. It looks chosen, not picked. Alignment is genuinely clean. Margins match across slides. Icons are theme-matched to the rest of the deck instead of pulled from a generic pack. Most AI tools default to a blue-and-white SaaS palette regardless of your prompt. Claude Design actually listens. The catch is data slides. The moment a slide needs to carry real analytical weight, multi-series charts, comparison tables with more than three columns, timelines with annotations, the output drops a tier. Labels stuff together (as seen below). Numbers sit on top of gridlines. Legends end up where you can't read them. Claude's full review of all three Claude presentation tools has the side-by-side examples and the cost-per-deck math: How to Use Claude to Create Presentations . The other thing nobody talks about: after five or six decks, Claude Design's house style becomes your house style. Same corner callouts, same editorial palette, same hierarchy. There's a research term for this. The 2024 Nature paper by Shumailov et al. calls it model collapse. For a one-off deck it doesn't matter. For anyone making more than two decks a month, it shows up fast. Key Features Slide Deck starting mode purpose-built for presentations (alongside prototype, template, freeform) Pre-build questionnaire of four to five clarifying questions before generation (audience, tone, visual direction, duration, angle) Inline comments for element-level edits without writing prompt paragraphs Direct element editing for manual content, color, size, and position changes Drawing-style annotation to sketch layout changes directly on the canvas Six export paths: PPTX, PDF, standalone HTML, send to Canva, .zip, hand off to Claude Code Design system setup for brand consistency (Team accounts only, admin permissions required) Pros Strongest typography and visual hierarchy of any native Claude tool Inline comments make iteration fast: 20 to 40 seconds per edit Layouts feel intentional, not templated Works directly in claude.ai with no install Theme actually matches your prompt instead of defaulting to the house style Six export paths cover most handoff workflows Cons Slowest first generation of any Claude option (around 15 minutes including the questionnaire) Charts and data slides render visibly worse than the rest of the deck Presentation-specific layouts (Funnel, Feature Matrix, Compare Two, Hub & Spoke) aren't in the default set The questionnaire adds friction before generation, especially when your prompt is already detailed Design system setup requires a Team account with admin permissions Output sameness kicks in after five-plus decks Not built for sales or business presentations Who It's For Founders building a one-off investor teaser. Marketers shipping a keynote deck or a think piece. Anyone who needs one beautiful presentation, not a recurring workflow. If you already pay for Claude Pro for research or writing, Claude Design comes with it. You don't need a separate subscription. When to Choose Claude Design Choose it when typography and visual hierarchy matter more than data density. Skip it if your deck depends on charts, if you're shipping more than two decks, or if you need true brand template preservation without setting up a Team account. For data-heavy decks or anything sales-facing, the other tools in this list will get you closer faster. Pricing Plan Price Best for Pro $17/mo annual, $20/mo monthly Quick explorations, one-off decks Max 5x From $100/mo Semi-regular use: PMs, engineers building regular mock-ups Max 20x $200/mo Power use: designers and creatives Team Standard $20/seat/mo annual, min 5 seats Quick exploration across a team Team Premium $100/seat/mo annual, min 5 seats Power users: in-house designers Enterprise Custom (contact sales) Usage-based billing at API rates Anthropic doesn't publish exact credit counts or slide-count limits per tier. Allowances are per user, not pooled at the org level. Claude Design is still a research preview, so usage tracking and audit logs aren't available yet. Worth knowing if you're in a regulated environment. Final Summary: How to Choose the Right AI Presentation Tool If You're Looking For… Recommended Tool Runner-Up Best AI for enterprise teams Alai Prezent.ai Best AI for business Alai Prezent.ai Best free AI presentation maker Gamma Canva Best AI for design teams Chronicle / Canva Beautiful.ai Best AI for research-heavy decks Manus AI Genspark AI Best AI for sales decks (with analytics) Pitch Alai Best AI for Google Slides users Plus AI Gemini Canvas Best AI for PowerPoint users Plus AI Alai Best budget AI presentation maker SlidesAI Gamma Best AI for pitch decks Alai Gamma Best AI for investor decks Alai Beautiful.ai Best AI for executive & board presentations Prezent.ai Alai Best AI for brand-consistent decks Alai Beautiful.ai Best AI for consultants Alai Napkin AI Best AI for marketing teams Canva Alai Best AI for students Canva Gamma Best AI for teachers & educators Canva Prezi AI Best AI for fact-checked content Genspark AI Manus AI Best AI for infographics & diagrams Napkin AI Canva Best AI for converting YouTube/audio to slides NoteGPT SlidesGPT Best AI for interactive presentations Chronicle Prezi AI Best AI for Google Workspace power users Gemini Canvas Plus AI Best AI for one-off branded decks Claude Design Alai Quick Hits: 8 More AI Presentation Makers I Tested (That Did Not Make The Cut) These eight AI presentation makers did not make the main list but are worth knowing about if you have a specific use case the top 16 do not cover. Decktopus : Beginner-friendly AI PPT maker with form-based prompt entry. Output is functional but flat. Good for first-time AI presentation maker users who want a guided experience. MagicSlides : A Google Slides add-on that competes directly with Plus AI on price. Cheaper but design output is more basic. Worth testing if Plus AI's trial pricing puts you off. Slidesgo AI : From the Freepik team. Templates-first AI presentation maker with strong template variety but weak AI generation. The library is the value, not the AI. Wonderslide : Takes an existing PowerPoint deck and redesigns it. Useful for upgrading old PPT files rather than generating new ones from scratch. Presentations.AI : Enterprise-positioned with team collaboration features. Pricing is opaque and the free tier is limited. Worth a demo if Beautiful AI is too expensive. Slideoo : Newer entrant with a focus on speed. Generates decks in under two minutes. Design output trails the top tier. Simplified : General design suite that includes AI presentation generation as one of many features. Similar positioning to Canva but smaller template library. Designs.ai : Old-school AI design platform that has bolted on presentation generation. Output feels dated compared to native AI presentation makers like Alai or Gamma. What I Learned After Testing 16 AI Presentation Makers Here is what 16 hours of testing produced, in numbers. 4 of 16 tools produced broken PowerPoint exports that required more than 15 minutes of cleanup. Gamma, Pitch, Beautiful AI imports, and SlidesGPT all had formatting damage on the PPT round-trip. 2 of 16 tools ignored my source content entirely and generated their own deck on a vaguely related topic. NoteGPT and SlidesGPT both did this on the single-slide test. 3 of 16 tools have no PowerPoint export at all. Prezi AI (import only), Chronicle (PDF only), and Gemini Canvas (Google Slides only, no native PPT). If PowerPoint is your distribution format, those three are non-starters regardless of how good the editing experience feels. 1 of 16 produced four design variants per slide on the first prompt. Alai. Every other AI presentation maker gave a single result and asked me to regenerate if I wanted to try something different. 5 of 16 had no usable free tier. Beautiful AI, Plus AI (7-day trial only with card required), Prezent.ai (demo only), Manus AI (credits but limited), and SlidesGPT (view-only) all force payment or a sales call before you can produce a downloadable deck. The gap between AI-generated slides and designer-quality output has closed significantly in 2026. If you are still building every deck from scratch, you are leaving hours on the table. But the gap between the best AI presentation maker and the worst is still wide enough that picking the wrong one wastes more time than building manually would have. Parting Notes If you only try one tool: Start with Alai . The 4-options-per-slide approach solved my biggest frustration with AI presentation makers, which is endless regeneration until you get lucky. Agent Mode makes editing feel like having a design assistant who actually understands what you want. And for teams and enterprises, the full design system encoding means every deck looks consistent without anyone policing it manually. It is the only AI presentation tool that covers design quality, iteration speed, brand consistency, and scale in one place. If your decks are shared, not presented: Gamma is built for async. The scrollable web format works well for investor updates, internal reports, and any deck that gets viewed over email or Slack rather than in a meeting room. 400 free credits is hard to beat as a starting point. If you just want templates, not AI: Skip the AI hype and go with Beautiful AI or Canva . Beautiful AI is the better choice if brand consistency matters and you want design guardrails. Canva is better if you want massive variety and already use it for other design work. Both give you polished templates without relying on AI generation. If you live in Google Slides: Plus AI is the only tool that does not add friction to your existing workflow. The gap between AI-generated slides and designer-quality output has closed significantly. title: Tipos de alopecia: guía completa para identificar cuál tienes

body_text: ¿Se te cae el pelo y no sabes qué tipo de alopecia tienes? Notas más pelo en el desagüe. En la almohada. En el cepillo. Y lo primero que haces es buscar en Google "caída del cabello" — y te encuentras con un mar de información confusa, productos milagrosos y diagnósticos aterradores que no aplican a tu caso. La verdad es que existen más de 15 tipos de alopecia , cada uno con causas, tratamientos y pronósticos completamente diferentes. Lo que funciona para la calvicie por genética no sirve para la caída por estrés. El tratamiento para una tiroides desregulada no hace nada contra una alopecia areata. Tratar sin diagnosticar es tirar plata. Esta guía existe para que entiendas exactamente qué tipo de alopecia podrías tener , qué exámenes lo confirman y qué se puede hacer al respecto. Sin marketing. Sin "champú milagroso". Solo medicina. ¿Qué es la alopecia? (definición clara) Alopecia es el término médico para la pérdida de cabello , parcial o total, en cualquier zona del cuerpo. No es una enfermedad única — es un síntoma que puede venir de docenas de causas diferentes 1 . Es importante entender esto: alopecia no es sinónimo de calvicie irreversible . Muchos tipos de alopecia son reversibles si se tratan a tiempo. Otros se pueden frenar. Pero necesitas saber cuál tienes. Según la Clínica Universidad de los Andes, aproximadamente el 50% de los hombres y el 25% de las mujeres experimentarán algún tipo de alopecia significativa antes de los 50 años 2 . En Chile, los datos del MINSAL muestran que la caída del cabello por estrés es uno de los motivos dermatológicos más frecuentes de consulta. Clasificación de la alopecia: los 2 grandes grupos Los dermatólogos clasifican la alopecia en dos categorías fundamentales. Esta división es clave porque el abordaje diagnóstico y terapéutico es completamente distinto. 1. Alopecias cicatriciales (con destrucción folicular) El folículo piloso se destruye y es reemplazado por tejido cicatricial. El cabello no vuelve a crecer en las zonas afectadas. El objetivo del tratamiento es detener la propagación. 2. Alopecias no cicatriciales (sin destrucción folicular) El folículo sigue vivo pero no produce cabello (o produce cabello más fino). La mayoría son reversibles si se trata la causa subyacente. Representan más del 90% de los casos. Tipo ¿Cicatricial? ¿Reversible? Prevalencia Androgenética No Parcial (frenable) La más común (95% hombres) Efluvio telógeno No Sí, totalmente Muy común en mujeres Alopecia areata No Sí (con tratamiento) 2% de la población Por tracción Depende del tiempo Parcial Frecuente en mujeres Frontal fibrosante Sí No (frenable) Mujeres post-menopáusicas Infecciosa (tiña) No (si se trata pronto) Sí Niños y adolescentes Alopecia androgenética: la calvicie común (y la más tratable) Es responsable del 95% de los casos de alopecia en hombres y afecta también a un porcentaje significativo de mujeres. Es la que conoces como "calvicie de patrón" — entradas, coronilla, adelgazamiento progresivo. La causa es genética + hormonal. En personas con predisposición genética, la dihidrotestosterona (DHT) —un derivado de la testosterona— hace que los folículos se miniaturicen progresivamente: producen cabello cada vez más fino hasta que dejan de producirlo. Si quieres entender todos los detalles de este tipo —causas, grados según la escala Norwood/Hamilton, diagnóstico y tratamiento— lee nuestra guía completa de alopecia androgenética . Tratamientos disponibles para alopecia androgenética Minoxidil — tópico u oral, estimula crecimiento Finasterida — bloquea la conversión de testosterona a DHT Dutasterida — más potente que finasterida, bloquea ambos tipos de 5-alfa-reductasa Minoxidil + Finasterida combinados — efecto sinérgico Plasma rico en plaquetas (PRP) — estimula folículos dormant Trasplante capilar — para casos avanzados ¿Crees que tienes alopecia androgenética? Un dermatólogo puede confirmarlo en una consulta por telemedicina. Sin salir de casa. Agendar dermatología online → Efluvio telógeno: cuando el estrés hace que se caiga a manotazos El efluvio telógeno es la segunda causa más común de alopecia, especialmente en mujeres. Se reconoce porque el pelo se cae de forma difusa (no en parches ni en entradas) — notas que cae de todas partes de la cabeza. La causa: un evento de estrés físico o emocional hace que un porcentaje anormal de folículos entre en fase telógena (reposo) simultáneamente. De 2 a 3 meses después del evento detonante, el pelo empieza a caer masivamente. Detonantes comunes: Infecciones graves (incluyendo post-COVID ) Cirugías o hospitalizaciones Postparto (causa extremadamente común) Dietas extremas o pérdida de peso rápida Estrés emocional severo Problemas de tiroides Deficiencia de hierro/ferritina La buena noticia: el efluvio telógeno es autolimitado y reversible . Una vez que pasa el detonante, el cabello vuelve a crecer en 6-12 meses. Pero los exámenes de sangre son clave para descartar causas subyacentes que puedan prolongarlo. Alopecia areata: cuando el sistema inmune ataca el cabello La alopecia areata es una enfermedad autoinmune donde el cuerpo ataca sus propios folículos pilosos. Se presenta como parches redondos de calvicie súbita , a veces de la noche a la mañana. Afecta al 2% de la población y puede aparecer a cualquier edad. En casos severos puede progresar a alopecia totalis (pérdida de todo el cabello de la cabeza) o alopecia universalis (pérdida de todo el vello corporal). El diagnóstico es clínico —un dermatólogo lo reconoce a simple vista— pero los exámenes de sangre ayudan a descartar otras enfermedades autoinmunes asociadas (tiroiditis, vitíligo, diabetes tipo 1). Alopecia por tracción: el precio de peinados apretados Si usas colas de caballo muy tirantes, trenzas apretadas, extensiones o alisados con tensión constante, estás sometiendo los folículos a una fuerza mecánica sostenida. Con el tiempo, esto produce recesión de la línea frontal y pérdida de cabello en las zonas de mayor tensión. Si se detecta temprano, es totalmente reversible cambiando el peinado. Pero si la tensión continúa por años, los folículos se dañan permanentemente y se vuelve cicatricial. Alopecia frontal fibrosante: la que afecta a mujeres post-menopáusicas Es una alopecia cicatricial que afecta predominantemente a mujeres mayores de 50 años . Se caracteriza por recesión progresiva de la línea frontal —la frente se hace cada vez más amplia— acompañada de pérdida de cejas en algunos casos. Es un tipo de alopecia relativamente nuevo en la literatura médica (descrita en 1994) y su incidencia va en aumento. No tiene cura, pero el tratamiento precoz con antiinflamatorios tópicos y sistémicos puede frenar su progresión 3 . Alopecia por hongos (tiña capitis): común en niños Los hongos en el cuero cabelludo pueden causar pérdida de cabello en parches, especialmente en niños y adolescentes. Se presenta con descamación, enrojecimiento y cabello quebradizo que se rompe a nivel del cuero cabelludo. Se trata con antifúngicos y el cabello vuelve a crecer una vez eliminada la infección. Si no se trata, puede dejar cicatrices y pérdida permanente. Otros tipos menos comunes de alopecia Tricotilomanía Trastorno del control de impulsos donde la persona se arranca el cabello compulsivamente. Causa parches irregulares de alopecia con cabello de diferentes longitudes. Tratamos este tema en profundidad aquí — es más común de lo que crees y tiene 70,000+ búsquedas mensuales en Chile. Alopecia cicatricial por lupus El lupus eritematoso sistémico puede causar alopecia cicatricial en cuero cabelludo. Se manifiesta como parches con eritema, descamación y atrofia. Requiere manejo reumatológico + dermatológico. Alopecia por deficiencias nutricionales No solo el hierro bajo causa caída. Las deficiencias de biotina , zinc, vitamina D, vitamina B12 y proteínas también pueden provocar efluvio telógeno. Los alimentos para fortalecer el cabello son la primera línea de prevención. Alopecia por medicamentos Anticoagulantes, betabloqueadores, antidepresivos, retinoides y quimioterapia son causas farmacológicas comunes. La caída suele revertirse al suspender o cambiar el medicamento (excepto en quimioterapia, donde el patrón es diferente). "¿Cómo sé qué tipo de alopecia tengo?" — Tabla diagnóstica Esta tabla te ayuda a orientarte, pero no reemplaza un diagnóstico médico . Un dermatólogo puede confirmar el tipo de alopecia con tricoscopia (examen del cuero cabelludo con aumento) y exámenes de sangre. Patrón de caída Más probable Edad típica Acción Entradas + coronilla (hombres) Androgenética 25-50+ Consultar dermatología, iniciar finasterida/minoxidil Adelgazamiento difuso coronilla (mujeres) Androgenética femenina 30-60+ Exámenes hormonales + dermatología Caída masiva difusa (manotazos) Efluvio telógeno Cualquiera Exámenes de sangre (TSH, ferritina, hemograma) Parche(s) redondo(s) súbitos Alopecia areata Cualquiera Dermatología urgente (mejor pronóstico con tratamiento precoz) Línea frontal retrocede (mujer 50+) Frontal fibrosante 50-70 Dermatología urgente (cicatricial, hay que frenarlo) Caída + descamación/caspa Tiña / dermatitis seborreica Niños (tiña), adultos (DS) Examen micológico + antifúngico Cejas se caen + cansancio Hipotiroidismo 30-60 Examen TSH urgent 💡 Dato clave: El 80% de las personas que se autodiagnostican alopecia en Internet se equivocan de tipo. Y tratar el tipo equivocado no solo no funciona — puede empeorar las cosas. Un dermatólogo puede diagnosticar el tipo correcto en una sola consulta. ¿Qué exámenes de sangre pedir para diagnosticar alopecia? Los exámenes de sangre para caída del cabello varían según el tipo sospechado, pero el panel básico incluye: Hemograma completo — descarta anemia Ferritina — mide reservas de hierro (debe estar sobre 50 ng/mL) TSH y T4 libre — descarta disfunción tiroidea Hierro sérico — complementa la ferritina Vitamina D — deficiencia se asocia con varios tipos de alopecia Zinc y B12 — deficiencias nutricionales Hormonas (si sospecha androgenética en mujer) — testosterona, DHEA-S, prolactina En Examedi podemos tomar todos estos exámenes de sangre a domicilio , sin necesidad de ir a un laboratorio. Resultidos en 24-48 horas. ¿Qué tipo de alopecia es más peligrosa? Esta es una pregunta de miedo común. La respuesta corta: ningún tipo de alopecia es peligrosa para tu salud física general . Ninguna pone en riesgo tu vida. La alopecia es un problema dermatológico, no una enfermedad sistémica (con la excepción de cuando es síntoma de otra condición como lupus o problema tiroideo). Sin embargo, las alopecias cicatriciales (frontal fibrosante, lupus, algunas por tracción crónica) son las que más preocupan porque producen pérdida permanente e irreversible. En estos casos, el tiempo es crítico: cuanto antes se diagnostiquen y traten, más folículos se salvan. Para tu salud mental y autoestima, todos los tipos de alopecia pueden ser significativamente impactantes. El estrés por la caída del cabello puede incluso empeorar la caída (ciclo vicioso). No minimices el impacto emocional. El diagnóstico correcto lo cambia todo No gastes en productos sin saber qué tipo tienes. Exámenes de sangre a domicilio en 24-48h. Solicitar exámenes → Preguntas frecuentes ¿Cuántos tipos de alopecia existen? Existen más de 15 tipos de alopecia reconocidos médicamente. Se dividen en dos grandes grupos: no cicatriciales (androgenética, efluvio telógeno, areata, por tracción) y cicatriciales (frontal fibrosante, por lupus, foliculitis declipante). Las no cicatriciales son las más comunes y representan más del 90% de los casos. ¿Qué tipo de alopecia es reversible? La mayoría de las alopecias no cicatriciales son reversibles o al menos frenables. El efluvio telógeno es totalmente reversible una vez que se resuelve la causa. La alopecia areata tiene alta tasa de recuperación con tratamiento. La androgenética no es reversible pero se puede frenar significativamente con minoxidil, finasterida o dutasterida. ¿Cómo sé si mi alopecia es por estrés? La alopecia por estrés (efluvio telógeno) se caracteriza por caída difusa —de todas partes de la cabeza, no en parches ni en entradas— que aparece 2-3 meses después de un evento estresante (embarazo, cirugía, infección, estrés emocional severo). Si notas este patrón, los exámenes de sangre ayudan a confirmarlo descartando otras causas. ¿La alopecia areata es peligrosa? No, no es peligrosa para tu salud general. Es una condición autoinmune donde el cuerpo ataca los folículos pilosos. No afecta otros órganos en la mayoría de los casos. Sin embargo, se asocia con mayor frecuencia de otras condiciones autoinmunes (tiroiditis, vitíligo), por lo que tu médico puede pedir exámenes adicionales. ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre alopecia y calvicie? La alopecia es el término médico para cualquier tipo de pérdida de cabello. La calvicie es el resultado visible de ciertos tipos de alopecia (principalmente la androgenética). No todas las alopecias producen calvicie: muchas son temporales o reversibles si se tratan a tiempo. ¿Puedo prevenir la alopecia androgenética si la detecto temprano? No se puede prevenir completamente porque tiene base genética, pero detectarla temprano permite iniciar tratamiento antes de que los folículos se miniaturicen completamente. Con finasterida o dutasterida + minoxidil, la mayoría de los pacientes mantienen su cabello por años o décadas. La clave es empezar antes de que la pérdida sea visible. Bibliografía MedlinePlus. Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology , 2020. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33157088/ Mayo Clinic. title: Naïve Raises $28.5M to Let AI Agents Run Companies
summary: Fundraise Insider tracks newly funded startups each week and delivers verified sales leads of C-suite contacts straight to your inbox, so you reach the right
body_text: Fundraise Insider tracks newly funded startups each week and delivers verified sales leads of C-suite contacts straight to your inbox, so you reach the right people while the funding is still fresh. See pricing. Naïve has raised $28.5 million in a Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners. The San Francisco, California company sells infrastructure that lets AI agents handle the bulk of the work involved in setting up and running a business. The company has signed up more than 30,000 developer customers within months of launching, and annual run rate revenue has grown tenfold over the past six months to the low double digit millions. What Naïve does is bundle the tedious parts of company formation and operation behind a single API. Payments, email accounts, phone numbers, cloud infrastructure, storage and incorporation all sit behind one interface. Developers hand a prompt to tools such as Cursor, Claude Code or Codex, which connect to the API and provision what is needed. An agent can orchestrate the formation of a US LLC by supplying the state, industry code, business description and proposed names, though a human is still required to complete KYC and KYB checks and make any payments. From there the agents can set up inboxes, virtual cards, phone numbers, databases and compute, plus connections to services including Stripe and QuickBooks. A governance layer lets users set budgets, limit what their agents are allowed to do, and require human sign off before sensitive actions go through. Naïve also ships templates for common business types, among them AI SEO, full stack SaaS apps, recruiting, accounting and customer support, along with a mobile emulator that lets agents operate smartphone apps on emulated devices. Customers are using it for AI automation agencies, faceless content channels on TikTok and YouTube, and in one case a rental car agency running autonomously. AI automation agencies are currently the fastest growing category. The second half of the opportunity is cost. Agents that call expensive models, pass large amounts of context between tasks and consume resources while idle get expensive quickly. Naïve is putting some of the new capital into a model router that sends queries to the most efficient model for a given task while preserving and replaying reasoning already done, a memory system that surfaces business context on demand, and an orchestrator that divides work among agents. It is also building a serverless runtime that runs agents inside lightweight JavaScript environments rather than giving each one a full virtual machine, so customers pay mainly when an agent is actually working. Naïve was founded by Sean Dorje and Dennis Zax, both 20, who dropped out of Berkeley and had been building software together since they were 14. They sold their previous company, ezML, as teenagers before joining Y Combinator. Y Combinator, Zetta, Liquid 2 and angel investors including Gokul Rajaram, Apollo.io co-founder Tim Zheng and former HubSpot COO JD Sherman also joined the round, which brings total capital raised to roughly $32 million. The company has 10 full time employees, and proceeds will go toward hiring researchers and developing its four infrastructure projects: virtualized sandboxes for agents, model routing and inference optimization, a memory layer, and governance and orchestration.

title: JPMorganChase, Official Bank of Team USA and the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games, doubles down on Southern California with expanded small business support
body_text: Press Releases JPMorganChase, Official Bank of Team USA and the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games, doubles down on Southern California with expanded small business support Nearly 30% increase in business bankers and plans to expand its Coaching for Impact program to graduate more than 3,700 additional entrepreneurs across Greater Los Angeles and Riverside over the next five years. More than $1 million in new philanthropic funding to strengthen Los Angeles’ small business ecosystem, building on more than $15 million deployed since 2020. Plans to open a new Community Center Branch in East LA next month—the 2nd in Los Angeles and 20th across the nation—deepening support for local entrepreneurs and residents. LOS ANGELES August 05, 2026 JPMorganChase, the Official Bank of Team USA and the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games (LA28 Games) and a Founding Partner of the LA28 Games, today announced a significant expansion of its support for small businesses across Southern California—including Greater Los Angeles and Riverside. Over the next five years, the firm will hire more than 100 additional business bankers across the region—a nearly 30% increase—and plans to scale its Coaching for Impact program to graduate more than 3,700 additional local entrepreneurs. The firm will also open a new Community Center Branch in East Los Angeles next month, its 2nd in Los Angeles and 20th in the nation, deepening support for the neighborhood and connecting local entrepreneurs directly to financial education programming and resources. In Los Angeles and across Southern California, the firm will deploy more than $1 million in new philanthropic funding to help expand procurement readiness and supplier connections, strengthen access to capital and business coaching and support community-based financial empowerment for small business owners, helping more local entrepreneurs grow and compete for opportunities tied to the LA28 Games. This new funding will help support over 120 local businesses and builds on more than $15 million deployed since 2020 to strengthen the small business ecosystem in Los Angeles. This work in Southern California is part of the firm’s American Dream Initiative, a multi-year effort to scale effective solutions that help expand opportunity in communities and includes scaling firmwide support for 10 million small businesses nationwide—up from seven million served today. “Entrepreneurs fuel the local economy, and their small businesses create jobs, strengthen communities and drive long-term growth across Southern California,” said Diedra Porché, Head of Community and Business Development and Regional Chair of the California and West Market Leadership Teams at JPMorganChase. “Following our announcement as the Official Bank of Team USA and the LA28 Games, and a Founding Partner of the LA28 Games, we’re focused on ensuring small businesses across the region benefit from this enormous opportunity. By combining philanthropic funding with the credit, capital and support small businesses need, we’re helping entrepreneurs navigate complex contracting processes and compete before and after the LA28 Games.” Expanding capacity for growth through coaching and local business banking JPMorganChase’s Coaching for Impact program provides complimentary one-on-one consulting, executive coaching and on demand education to help small businesses strengthen operations, improve credit readiness and drive growth at every stage. Nationwide, more than 15,000 entrepreneurs have graduated from the program since its launch—including more than 900 across Greater Los Angeles and Riverside. The firm plans to increase its local business banker coverage by nearly 30% over the next five years—these bankers work directly with entrepreneurs, providing financial advice, access to capital and connections to valuable resources that help small businesses invest, expand and navigate economic hurdles. “We know that many small business owners operate with only a few weeks of cash on hand, making it harder to manage day-to-day expenses while preparing for larger opportunities to grow their businesses around global events,” said Stevie Baron, CEO of Chase for Business. “That’s why we’re focused on connecting local entrepreneurs in Southern California to capital and resources that build resilience and help them navigate procurement pathways so more businesses are ready to compete for and deliver on major contracts.” Growing our footprint to expand financial education Next month, JPMorganChase will open a new Community Center Branch in East LA to expand support for local entrepreneurs and residents. The branch will feature a community room that can be used after hours, free Wi Fi and dedicated space for “One Chase” partners across banking, lending and investments—alongside local artwork and bilingual Spanish/English signage that reflect the neighborhood. A Community Center Manager and Coaching for Impact consultant will be on-site to provide one-on-one guidance, workshops and tailored support to help entrepreneurs grow and build lasting wealth for the community. Since the first Community Branch opened in 2019, these branches have served as neighborhood hubs for financial education and resources that promote financial security, small business growth and homeownership. With nearly 120,000 residents—more than 95% identifying as Hispanic or Latino, over 80% speaking a language other than English at home and nearly 40% foreign-born—East LA is a community where culturally relevant programming and trusted partnerships can make a meaningful impact. Strengthening Los Angeles small businesses ahead of the LA28 Games In Los Angeles, JPMorganChase will provide more than $1 million in new philanthropic funding to local organizations to help strengthen the small business ecosystem and support entrepreneurs as they pursue major procurement opportunities, like those related to the LA28 Games—helping build a stronger pipeline of Los Angeles-based suppliers for contracting opportunities that can support the broader Southern California region. Among the organizations supported are: Los Angeles Business Council Institute (LABCi): Expanding and improving Compete4LA, an online database connecting nearly 40,000 local small businesses to procurement opportunities—including driving suppliers toward RAMP (Regional Alliance Marketplace for Procurement), the City of LA’s procurement platform for all LA28 contracts and opportunities. Pacific Asian Consortium in Employment (PACE): Supporting operations for the City of LA’s ProcureLA initiative, which provides end-to-end support and connects small businesses to financing and contracting opportunities, including working capital to execute on awarded contracts. With this new round of funding, ProcureLA is expected to serve 120 additional small businesses, assist 60 in obtaining critical certifications and help businesses secure $7.5 million in awarded contracts, advancing the organization’s decades-long dedication to helping small businesses access procurement opportunities and drive local economic growth. “Compete4LA levels the playing field by making Los Angeles small businesses more visible to buyers,” said Mary Leslie, President of the Los Angeles Business Council (LABC) and LABC Institute. “JPMorganChase’s support helped us get this first-of-its-kind mappable, searchable database off the ground. Now, we’re building on that foundation with new programs that give small businesses direct access to prime contractors, City and County agencies, and major employers. Together, these tools give more local businesses access to game-changing contracting opportunities and help them build lasting economic resilience in their communities.” Impact in action The firm’s philanthropic investments are already making a measurable difference for local small businesses. LISC LA, a local nonprofit organization supporting community and economic development across Los Angeles, has strengthened its signature small business growth program, Ascend LA, with support from JPMorganChase. Ascend LA helps small businesses strengthen their operations, access capital, prepare for procurement opportunities, navigate contracts, develop competitive bids and pursue relevant certifications. Since launching in 2020, Ascend LA has graduated 260 businesses and helped participants secure more than $81.6 million in contract and bonding outcomes. These results have helped Los Angeles businesses build resilience, expand capacity and scale for long-term growth. “Small businesses do not lack ambition or ideas; they often need the right relationships, resources, and opportunities at the right moment,” said Jabbar Wesley, Senior Program Officer and Head of Economic Development at LISC LA. “JPMorganChase’s longstanding support has helped Ascend LA connect entrepreneurs with the expertise, capital, procurement pathways, and strategic relationships needed to compete for larger opportunities, create jobs, and building lasting wealth in their communities.” JPMorganChase has also funded initiatives like Get in the Game, led by the Los Angeles Area Chamber of Commerce and Next Street, a small business solutions firm. Launched in 2021, the initiative works to strengthen Los Angeles’ small business ecosystem by helping local suppliers get procurement-ready and connect to major contracting opportunities. The firm’s support included funding research by Get in the Game that identified an estimated $2 billion regional supplier capital gap and highlighted procurement bottlenecks that can limit small business growth. It also helped establish a coalition of organizations focused on strengthening the regional supplier ecosystem and driving long-term success for small businesses. Building on our longstanding dedication to Los Angeles JPMorganChase has served Greater Los Angeles for more than 135 years, helping to drive a prosperous economy that creates jobs, supports businesses and helps families thrive. The firm has over 330 branches serving more than 5.1 million consumer customers and 600,000 small business clients and provides credit, financing, treasury and payment solutions for businesses across various industries in the region. The firm has spent significant time with clients, customers, policymakers and community leaders across Los Angeles to strategically deploy resources, including more than $9 million in philanthropic contributions in support of wildfire recovery since January 2025. As the Official Bank of Team USA and the LA28 Games and a Founding Partner of the LA28 Games, JPMorganChase will help create opportunities for athletes, empower small businesses and invest in local communities. About JPMorganChase JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM) is a leading financial services firm based in the United States of America (“U.S.”), with operations worldwide. JPMorganChase had $5.0 trillion in assets and $375 billion in stockholders’ equity as of June 30, 2026. The Firm is a leader in investment banking, financial services for consumers and small businesses, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management. Under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands, the Firm serves millions of customers in the U.S., and many of the world’s most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients globally. Information about JPMorgan Chase & Co. is available at www.jpmorganchase.com . About the American Dream Initiative JPMorganChase’s American Dream Initiative is a multi-year effort to expand economic opportunity by scaling evidence-based solutions that help the economy work for more people. Through the Initiative, the firm will provide financing, facilitate capital, offer advice, training and tools, and advocate for policy solutions to help people start and grow small businesses, find affordable places to live, save and plan for their financial futures, get good jobs, access quality healthcare and strengthen local institutions. For more information on the American Dream Initiative, visit www.jpmorganchase.com/America .

title: 6 Simple Food Swaps to Cut Down on Ultra-Processed Foods

body_text: Discover six simple food swaps that can help you eat fewer ultra-processed foods, from homemade ice cream and tomato sauce to oat bars and popcorn. Ultra-processed foods are everywhere. From packaged snacks and ready-made sauces to sweet treats and convenience meals, they can make eating quickly and cheaply much easier. The problem is that many people want to reduce their intake of these foods but are unsure where to begin. The good news is that you do not need to completely change your diet overnight. A few practical food swaps can make everyday meals and snacks simpler while helping you rely more on familiar, minimally processed ingredients. Here are six easy ideas to try at home. 1. Swap conventional ice cream for a banana-based treat Ice cream can be an occasional part of a balanced diet, but some commercial products contain a long list of ingredients, including stabilisers, emulsifiers and flavouring agents. A simple alternative is frozen banana ice cream. Freeze ripe bananas, then blend them until smooth. Adding unsweetened cocoa powder creates a chocolate flavour, while peanut butter can provide extra creaminess. You can also blend frozen yoghurt with fruit for another easy dessert. Strawberries, peaches, berries and bananas can all work well. This approach has another advantage: it is a useful way to use fruit that is becoming overripe rather than throwing it away. The result may not taste exactly like traditional ice cream, but it can satisfy a craving for something cold, sweet and creamy without requiring a complicated recipe. 2. Make quick homemade bagels Bread products vary considerably in their ingredients and processing methods. If you regularly buy bagels, making a simple version at home can give you more control over what goes into them. One easy recipe uses self-raising flour and yoghurt as the main ingredients. Combine the two, shape the dough into bagels and cook them in an air fryer or oven. You can add a small amount of salt or experiment with seeds and herbs for additional flavour. Homemade bagels are also convenient because the dough can be prepared ahead of time. Once you have a recipe you like, you can make several portions and save them for future meals. Importantly, not every packaged bread product should automatically be considered unhealthy. Processing alone does not determine whether a food is nutritious. Overall diet, ingredients, portion size and frequency of consumption all matter. 3. Replace jarred tomato sauce with a simple homemade version Ready-made tomato sauces can be convenient, but some contain added sugar, preservatives, thickeners or other ingredients that you may prefer to avoid. Making your own sauce can be surprisingly straightforward. Start by gently cooking chopped onion and garlic in a little oil. Add passata or canned tomatoes, then stir in fresh or dried herbs. Allow everything to simmer for around 10 to 20 minutes. You can adjust the flavour to suit your meal by adding black pepper, chilli, basil or oregano. The biggest benefit is control. You know exactly what has gone into the sauce, and you can prepare enough to use across several meals. If you do buy tomato sauce, check the ingredient list. A simple product containing tomatoes, oil, herbs and salt may be a relatively straightforward choice. 4. Make your own stir-fry sauce Stir-fries are often considered a quick and nutritious meal, but the sauce can sometimes add significant amounts of sugar and salt. Instead of using a packaged sauce, try making your own combination at home. A basic mixture could include soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil and a small amount of honey. You can adjust the quantities according to your taste and add ginger, chilli or lime for more flavour. Because you are preparing the sauce yourself, you can also control how much you use. Soy sauce can be high in sodium, so people who need to monitor their salt intake may want to choose a reduced-salt variety or use a smaller quantity. The wider lesson is that sauces and seasonings can dramatically change a meal. Simple ingredients can often provide plenty of flavour without requiring a complicated recipe. 5. Choose homemade popcorn instead of heavily flavoured snacks Not every packet of crisps is necessarily ultra-processed, but many popular snack foods contain combinations of refined ingredients, flavourings and additives. Popcorn offers a simple alternative. Popcorn kernels can be heated on the hob or in a microwave-safe container with a suitable lid. Once the kernels have popped, you can add a small amount of salt, herbs or another seasoning. Popcorn is a whole-grain food and naturally contains fibre. However, preparation matters. Large quantities of butter, oil or salt can significantly change its nutritional profile. There is also an important safety consideration. Popcorn can be a choking hazard for young children and should not be given to children under five, according to NHS guidance. For adults and older children, homemade popcorn can be an inexpensive snack that is quick to prepare and easy to customise. 6. Make your own oat bars Granola, energy and protein bars are marketed as convenient healthy snacks, but their nutritional quality varies widely. A homemade oat bar gives you the opportunity to choose the ingredients yourself. Start with rolled oats, then add chopped nuts and dried fruit. Mashed banana can help bind the mixture while providing natural sweetness. Peanut or almond butter can add flavour and help create a softer texture. You can bake the mixture for roughly 18 to 20 minutes, depending on the recipe, or experiment with a chilled version that sets in the refrigerator or freezer. Rolled oats are whole grains and provide fibre. Nuts can contribute protein, unsaturated fats and other nutrients, although they are also energy-dense, so portion size remains important. Homemade oat bars can also be economical because you can use ingredients already sitting in your kitchen cupboards. You do not have to eliminate every ultra-processed food Reducing ultra-processed foods does not have to mean avoiding every packaged product. Some foods classified as ultra-processed can still have a place in an overall balanced diet, and the health effects of food processing are more complicated than simply labelling individual products as good or bad. A practical strategy is to focus on what you can add to your diet. More vegetables, fruit, whole grains, beans, nuts and other minimally processed foods can naturally reduce the amount of less nutritious food you eat. Small substitutions may therefore be more realistic than attempting a complete dietary overhaul. Instead of changing everything at once, start with one habit. Make homemade tomato sauce this week, prepare popcorn for your next snack or try a simple banana-based dessert. Over time, these small changes can make cooking from basic ingredients easier and more familiar. Final thoughts The easiest way to reduce ultra-processed food intake is often not to focus on restriction, but on practical alternatives. Homemade ice cream, simple bagels, tomato sauce, stir-fry dressing, popcorn and oat bars can all be prepared with relatively few ingredients. They also give you greater control over added sugar, salt, flavourings and other ingredients. You do not need a perfect diet. Building more meals and snacks around simple, recognisable ingredients can be a realistic first step toward a more varied and balanced eating pattern. Source: BBC Future's article, published 2 August 2026. Disclaimer: This article is for general educational and informational purposes only. It is not medical or nutritional advice and should not replace guidance from a qualified doctor, registered dietitian or other healthcare professional. Individual dietary needs vary, particularly for people with allergies, medical conditions or specific nutritional requirements.

title: Hackea el dólar con Nubank: Por qué la acción más negociada en Colombia está en la mira
summary: Hoy le vamos a poner la lupa a la consentida del Mercado Global Colombiano: NUCO
body_text: Hackea el dólar con Nubank: Por qué la acción más negociada en Colombia está en la mira Si estás pendiente del mercado, seguro sabes que el dólar en Colombia ha venido bajando. Y como ya lo hemos hablado, cuando el dólar baja la guardia, tus pesos ganan poder para comprar acciones de gigantes globales a precio de rebaja. Hoy le vamos a poner la lupa a la consentida del Mercado Global Colombiano: NUCO (Nubank) , que se mantiene como la acción internacional más negociada por los inversionistas en el país a través de la Bolsa de Valores de Colombia. Te voy a contar, sin enredos y respaldado en análisis financieros, qué está pasando con Nubank en la bolsa y por qué la caída del dólar hace que esta jugada en pesos se ponga aún más interesante. Doble descuento: Precio de la acción + Dólar abajo Para entender la oportunidad hay que mirar dos variables: el precio del activo en dólares y la tasa de cambio aquí en Colombia. Descuento en la acción: Tras venir de máximos históricos, la acción de Nu Holdings (NU) tuvo una corrección en Wall Street que la llevó a cotizar en la zona de los 12 a 13 dólares, buscando estabilizarse recientemente entre los 13,50 y 14 dólares. Descuento en el dólar: Al mismo tiempo, el dólar en Colombia ha caído. Eso significa que necesitas menos pesos para comprar la misma exposición internacional. Aquí te explicamos con más detalle sobre este comportamiento. Básicamente, estás ante un escenario donde la empresa tuvo un ajuste en su precio de cotización afuera y, al mismo tiempo, el tipo de cambio local te beneficia para entrar con menos pesos desde trii. ¿Por qué cayó la acción si el negocio sigue ganando plata? Es normal preguntarse: ¿si la empresa es tan grande, por qué bajó en bolsa? La respuesta corta es que las expectativas de Wall Street eran altísimas. Aunque Nubank sigue generando utilidades netas gigantescas (superando los 870 millones de dólares en un solo trimestre), el ajuste en el precio se dio por tres razones principales: Más reservas para protección (provisiones): De acuerdo con análisis de Bloomberg Línea , al aumentar ligeramente la cartera vencida, Nubank guardó más dinero como escudo para cubrir posibles impagos. La compañía aclaró que esto busca proteger la cartera a largo plazo, aunque apretó un poco los márgenes a corto plazo. Tasas de interés que no bajan tan rápido: Un reporte de EBC señala que las tasas de interés en América Latina no bajaron al ritmo proyectado, lo que encarece el costo de financiamiento y exige mayor cautela al prestar dinero sin garantías (como tarjetas de crédito). Inversión para crecer: Expandir el negocio de forma agresiva en México y Colombia requiere inversiones iniciales altas mientras los portafolios de clientes maduran. Los datos duros que demuestran la fuerza de Nu A pesar del ajuste en el precio de la acción, la operación de Nubank no para de romper marcas y acumular hitos operativos: Licencia bancaria completa en México: La CNBV les dio la autorización final para pasar de SOFIPO a banco completo en México, lo que les permite ampliar su oferta y reducir sus costos de captación. Más de 15 millones de clientes en México: Ya alcanzaron el punto de equilibrio operativo en ese país, consolidándose como una de las entidades financieras más grandes por número de usuarios. Compra estratégica en Brasil: Tal como reportó el diario La República , Nu Holdings acordó la adquisición de Banco Porto Real para fortalecer su división de banca de inversión y servicios patrimionales. Inteligencia Artificial de alto nivel: David Vélez, CEO de Nubank, fue nombrado en el consejo directivo de OpenAI, reforzando la apuesta del banco por reestructurar la banca usando inteligencia artificial. ¿Qué dicen los analistas de Wall Street? Para los grandes analistas de instituciones financieras internacionales, el aumento en las reservas no es un deterioro estructural del negocio, sino un blindaje deliberado y prudente para continuar creciendo con seguridad. De hecho, datos de Investing.com muestran que la mayoría de firmas de análisis mantienen una perspectiva de largo plazo alcista (con precios objetivo en el rango de 16 a 18 dólares), respaldada por un retorno sobre el patrimonio (ROE) sobresaliente proyectado cercano al 29% hacia los próximos años. Tú eliges cómo armar tu estrategia No necesitas abrir cuentas raras en el exterior, traducir formularios en inglés ni pagar comisiones por giros internacionales. Desde trii entras al Mercado Global Colombiano, buscas NUCO y te adueñas de tu participación directamente en pesos. Y recuerda: cada movimiento que haces te deja listo mientras sigues acumulando chances para la bolsa millonaria y construyes tu portafolio a tu propio ritmo. El dólar bajó la guardia y los gigantes globales están a un toque en tu celular. Aviso legal / Disclaimer: Este contenido es exclusivamente educativo e informativo y no constituye ni debe interpretarse como una recomendación, asesoramiento o sugerencia de inversión. Las rentabilidades pasadas no garantizan rendimientos futuros. Antes de tomar cualquier decisión financiera, analiza tu perfil de riesgo e investiga.

title: Loopio vs HeyIris (2026): A Neutral, Feature-by-Feature Comparison
summary: Loopio vs HeyIris compared on AI, pricing, integrations, and reviews - plus a newer AI-native alternative worth knowing before you buy.
body_text: Loopio vs HeyIris (2026): A Neutral, Feature-by-Feature Comparison Compared on AI, pricing, integrations, and reviews — plus a newer AI-native alternative worth knowing before you buy. Loopio vs HeyIris ~9 min read · Last reviewed Jan 2026 L Loopio Established RFP platform Library-first · governance vs HeyIris H AI-native assistant AI-first · fast drafting Figure 1 · A 2026 head-to-head: established platform vs AI-native assistant Last reviewed: January 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 and Capterra reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing and feature details change over time, so confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing. TL;DR: Loopio vs HeyIris Loopio fits teams that want an established response-management platform with a mature content library, structured workflows, and a large, proven review base. HeyIris fits teams that want an AI-native assistant built around fast, model-driven drafting rather than years of library maintenance. Which is better depends on what your team needs: Loopio leans toward governance and process maturity, HeyIris toward AI-first speed. Run both through the same real RFP before you commit to either. What Should You Consider When Choosing Between Loopio and HeyIris? Answer-first: weigh how each tool handles AI drafting, content governance, and total cost of ownership — not just headline features. Use these criteria to structure your demos. AI capabilities: Does the tool generate first drafts, or mainly retrieve existing answers? Test it on real questions. Content governance: Who keeps the library accurate, and how are outdated answers flagged? Conflict detection: Can the platform surface contradictory answers before they reach a buyer? Hallucination control: Does AI output ship with citations and confidence signals, or plain text? Narrative-style proposals: Can it produce prose responses, not just Q&A pairs? Content management: How much manual tagging and curation does the library require? Workflow automation: How are assignments, reminders, and approvals handled? Collaboration: How well do SMEs, reviewers, and owners work in parallel? Integrations: Does it connect to your CRM, content stores, and SSO? (See the integrations table below.) Security and compliance: SOC 2? SSO? A clear data-handling policy for AI? Analytics: Can you track win rates, cycle time, and content usage? Pricing: Both vendors quote custom pricing — model total cost carefully and confirm with Vendr. Ease of implementation: How long until the team is productive? Enterprise scalability: Does it hold up across many concurrent RFPs and teams? L Loopio: Overview, Features, Limitations, Pricing, Reviews Screenshot — via Loopio Loopio is an established response-management platform built around a central content library and structured workflows. It is used by proposal, bid, and sales teams to store approved answers, assign SME reviews, and assemble RFP, RFI, and security-questionnaire responses. Its differentiator is maturity: a large customer base and a review history that spans years. Best features (per vendor pages and reviews) Central content library with tagging and version tracking. Workflow automation for assignments, due dates, and reminders. Review and approval cycles that keep SMEs and owners aligned. Project and progress tracking across active responses. Integrations with common CRMs, Slack, and SSO providers. Analytics on content usage and project status. Screenshot — via Loopio Limitations (sourced from reviews and third-party analyses) Some reviewers cite meaningful time spent maintaining and curating the library — a recurring theme for buyers researching Loopio competitors for RFP management . AI features are layered onto a library-first architecture rather than built AI-native, per user reports; teams weighing that difference often read a Loopio vs Inventive AI breakdown . Reused Q&A pairs can feel generic when a response needs deal-specific narrative, per reviewer feedback. Onboarding and initial content setup can be time-consuming, per Capterra reviews. Pricing is quote-based and, per Vendr data, can scale up at enterprise tiers. Conflict detection relies largely on manual review rather than automated flagging. Pricing: Loopio does not publish list pricing; plans are quote-based. Confirm current figures via Vendr and directly with the vendor. Ratings and reviews: Loopio reports a large review base on G2 with a strong score commonly cited around 4.7/5 (confirm the current number). It also lists on Capterra and TrustRadius ; confirm current ratings on each site. “ The content library keeps our answers consistent and cuts duplicate work. Verbatim user quote · source: G2 “ It works well, but keeping the library current takes real effort from our team. Verbatim user quote · source: Capterra H HeyIris: Overview, Features, Limitations, Pricing, Reviews Screenshot — via HeyIris HeyIris is a newer, AI-native RFP and sales response assistant. Rather than centering the workflow on a curated library, it centers it on AI generation — drafting responses from connected knowledge and letting reviewers refine output. As a newer entrant, its review base is smaller than Loopio's, and buyers should test claims directly. Best features (per vendor pages and early reviews) AI generation as the primary drafting workflow, not an add-on. Faster first drafts on standard questions, per vendor materials. A lighter setup burden than library-first tools, per early user reports. Collaboration features for review and refinement. A growing integration set for CRM and content sources. A modern interface aimed at fast adoption. Limitations (sourced from reviews and vendor materials) As a newer product, the review base is small — fewer independent data points, so verify claims; buyers often scan HeyIris alternatives and competitors to widen the field. Security certifications and SLAs should be confirmed directly; documentation is thinner than an established vendor's.
